title: Bolton thumb and its hole in the trank (leather glove)
description: Hole: along the fold of the trank, round bottom, a V flap at the top freed by a curved slit that runs to a dot (h_D); h_TR and h_TR2 are the two lips of the slit. Thumb: wide oval with two lobes at the top and a cleft (C) on the fold axis; folded, the lobes sewn together make the tip; a slit from the side edge (Ps) to the dot takes the flap.

seams.why: the thumb is eased into the hole, round its base from notch to notch
the two lobes sewn together make the tip; their edges differ a little on the diagram
side of the thumb: the slit that takes the flap opens in the Ps..RL edge, at a point block glove computes

sewing: Thumb edge N1..Ps (through B) onto the hole edge h_TR2, h_V, h_TL, h_B, h_RM, 3 % longer than the hole; thumb slit Ps..dot onto the hole slit h_TR..h_D; lobes C..LL and RL..C sewn together.

provenance.source: The Shapes of Fabric, leather glove pattern (size about 7): control points read from the published diagram
provenance.rights: Seven hole points and twelve thumb points read from a published diagram, source cited; no drawing reproduced
provenance.notes: The thumb outline is in units of the thumb height (unit_scale gives mm at the reference hand). block glove fits it to the hole edge lengths rather than using unit_scale.
